title: uncork-sse-headroom-replay-and-delimiter-escape-sequencing-fix
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Several production incidents showed that under bursty clients + aggressive backpressure, SSE fragments could be emitted in very small chunks that broke partial JSON spans and interleaved function/tool call sentinels. This caused: 1) downstream JSON parse errors, 2) tool/function-call sentinel reordering, and 3) opaque partial outputs that the OpenAI-compat layer could not reconcile.

This PR introduces a lightweight cork/uncork headroom replay mechanism and canonical delimiter/escape sequencing to make SSE chunking resilient without increasing latency for normal traffic. Key ideas: cork headroom buffers small low-entropy fragments for up to N ms (configurable) and attempts an ordered replay when the next chunk arrives; span anchors (span_id + seq) are stamped on outbound SSE events to allow deterministic reassembly; delimiter and escape tokens are normalized at the framing layer ("data: " prefix handling and trailing newline normalization) so we avoid split-escape sequences (e.g., a backslash split across frames). We avoid full message coalescing to retain streaming semantics — corking is optimistically short and abandons replay if headroom exceeds threshold.

Compatibility: The OpenAI-compat shim maps the old "tool_call" sentinel to the canonical "function_call" tag and honors span anchors when reassembling. Integration tests emulate TCP split and delayed segments to verify reassembly and correct function/toolcall ordering.

What changed (high level): commit list below. Tests added: unit tests for escape normalization, e2e for bursty-client reassembly, and fuzz harness for random delimiter splits. Metrics: added sse.reassembly.attempts and sse.reassembly.success_rate; added logging note when cork is abandoned.

Risk and rollout: This touches the streaming framing layer and the OpenAI compat adapter. Feature guarded behind feature flag "sse_cork_headroom_v1"; rollout to canary, then full main. No customer-facing API changes.

Developer notes: headroom defaults to 8ms and max replay size 4KB. Operators can tune via runtime config. The approach minimizes cost and latency impact while removing a class of partial-JSON and sentinel-order bugs.
commits: feat(sse): introduce cork headroom buffer and replay path
fix(sse): canonicalize delimiter/escape sequencing in framing layer
chore(openai-compat): map tool_call->function_call and respect span anchors
test(sse): add e2e bursty-client reassembly test
perf: micro-optimizations to avoid extra copies during replay
docs: document sse_cork_headroom_v1 flag and tuning knobs
review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you explain how corking interacts with existing prefix KV cache? Concern about duplicate-capture of partial KV cache entries.

Priya Shah: Cork only operates at framing layer; it does not retain semantic KV cache entries. We added a separation boundary (framer -> runtime API) and unit tests that assert no duplicate cache insertions.
Marta López: Lint flagged a formatting nit in compat_adapter.go; please run gofmt (fixed in second commit).
Samir Ahmed: e2e failed on first run due to timing flakiness; added retry and tuned default headroom to 8ms (was 12ms). Verified green on rerun and approved.

release_notes:
- Fixes partial-JSON parse failures caused by micro-fragmented SSE chunks under bursty backpressure.
- Stabilizes function/tool-call sentinel ordering across split frames.
- Adds feature flag sse_cork_headroom_v1 and new metrics: sse.reassembly.attempts and sse.reassembly.success_rate.
